subject.title: Regression: WebChat "Read Aloud" 🔊 TTS button removed with no replacement

question: Should WebChat restore a browser-local read-aloud control, or should it expose configured gateway TTS through a supported per-message playback surface?
rationale: The prior browser-speech behavior was reportedly removed, while a gateway-backed replacement proposal was closed as not planned; source work alone cannot resolve the intended product and security boundary.

options.title: Sponsor gateway-backed playback
options.body: Define a narrow WebChat-to-gateway TTS playback contract and implement accessible per-message controls around configured TTS behavior.

options.title: Restore browser-local playback
options.body: Reintroduce a clearly labeled browser speech-synthesis control without coupling it to gateway Talk or TTS configuration.

options.title: Keep no built-in playback surface
options.body: Document the intentional removal and direct users to supported external accessibility tooling if native playback is outside WebChat scope.

recommendation.title: Sponsor gateway-backed playback
recommendation.body: Define a narrow WebChat-to-gateway TTS playback contract and implement accessible per-message controls around configured TTS behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Their prior report most directly describes the WebChat/Talk product-boundary ambiguity that this decision must resolve.
